titulo: Quiz — The first minute, five questions long
subtitulo: Where from, how long, first time, do you like it — and the question you hand back
introPt: A traveller gets through the standard opening of every Greek conversation and comes out of it with a recommendation.
cenario: A kafeneio in the afternoon, two tables close together, one coffee each.

dialogo.es: Από πού είσαι; Πρώτη φορά στην Ελλάδα;
dialogo.pt: Where are you from? First time in Greece?
dialogo.tts: Από πού είσαι; Πρώτη φορά στην Ελλάδα;

dialogo.es: Είμαι από το Λονδίνο. Πρώτη φορά, ναι. Μου αρέσει πολύ.
dialogo.pt: I'm from London. First time, yes. I like it a lot.
dialogo.tts: Είμαι από το Λονδίνο. Πρώτη φορά, ναι. Μου αρέσει πολύ.

dialogo.es: Πόσες μέρες θα μείνεις; Και πού πας μετά;
dialogo.pt: How many days are you staying? And where are you going next?
dialogo.tts: Πόσες μέρες θα μείνεις; Και πού πας μετά;

dialogo.es: Δέκα μέρες. Πάω στη Θεσσαλονίκη. Και από πού είστε;
dialogo.pt: Ten days. I'm going to Thessaloniki. And where are you from?
dialogo.tts: Δέκα μέρες. Πάω στη Θεσσαλονίκη. Και από πού είστε;

perguntas.pergunta: You are asked whether you are married two minutes after sitting down. That is:
opcoes: An intrusion you should deflect
The standard opening move of a politeness system built on closeness
A sign that the conversation is going somewhere you did not intend
Something only asked of foreigners
perguntas.explica: Research comparing the two describes Greek as oriented towards positive politeness — involvement, closeness — and English towards negative politeness — distance, non-imposition. The questions are the opening move of the first.

perguntas.pergunta: «Σου αρέσει η Ελλάδα;» — what is doing what in that sentence?
opcoes: You like Greece
Greece pleases you
Greece asks you
You are liked in Greece
perguntas.explica: The verb turns the sentence round: the thing does the pleasing. Which is why the answer keeps the same shape — μου αρέσει πολύ, and nothing built out of I.

perguntas.pergunta: Saying «I'm going to Macedonia» in Greece can be understood two opposite ways because:
opcoes: The word is offensive
Macedonia is the name of a Greek region as well as part of the neighbouring state's constitutional name
It is not a real place name in Greek
It is only used for the ancient kingdom
perguntas.explica: Μακεδονία is a Greek region with Thessaloniki as its capital, and the Prespa Agreement, in force since February 2019, set «Republic of North Macedonia» as the neighbour's constitutional name. Say the city and the ambiguity disappears.

perguntas.pergunta: What do the commercial English indexes actually measure in Greece?
opcoes: The English of the Greek population
The English of people who chose to sit an online test
The English taught in Greek schools
The English used at tourist counters
perguntas.explica: Respondents are self-selected, have internet access and lean towards people interested in languages — EF says so itself. Speaking is consistently the weakest of the four skills measured.

perguntas.pergunta: You have answered five questions and he has answered none. What now?
opcoes: Keep answering, it is polite
Hand one back — «Και από πού είστε;»
Switch to English to speed things up
Say goodbye before it gets personal
perguntas.explica: The returned question is what turns an interview into a conversation, and the answer you get is usually a village rather than a country — which is where the good part starts.
